bull_bear.body:
- Integrated model combining product design, sourcing, manufacturing, brand management and distribution, allowing the Group to serve institutional and trade customers while using online channels to widen reach and gather consumer feedback
- Dual brand architecture — Autofurnish and Mototrance provide differentiated consumer propositions within the automotive-accessories category
- Complementary dual route to market: the Company's B2B platform plus Golden Mace's B2C e-commerce platform
- In-house production capabilities supported by sourced merchandise, balancing control, breadth and speed to market
- Established B2B capabilities described as a platform for deeper customer engagement, repeat business and broader product placement
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Working-capital intensity and funding dependence — MD&A flags that inventory and receivables can absorb cash and increase funding costs. Inventories and trade receivables rose materially during FY 2025-26 on the higher operating base, operating activities used cash rather than generating it, and funding requirements were met through financing inflows. Borrowings rose sharply, inventory-turnover, receivables-turnover and net-capital-turnover ratios all fell by more than 25%, and the debt-service coverage ratio fell on substantially increased debt-service obligations. Mitigation cited: SKU-level inventory discipline, customer credit controls, collections and cash-flow monitoring.
- Raw-material and merchandise cost volatility / supply disruption — Input-price volatility or supply disruption may compress margins or delay fulfilment. The business combines in-house manufacturing with sourced merchandise, so both manufacturing inputs and bought-in goods are exposed. Mitigation cited: supplier diversification, demand planning, negotiated procurement and selective price actions.
- Customer and channel concentration — Dependence on large customers or online marketplaces can affect volumes, pricing and visibility. The Company is primarily B2B while its subsidiary's B2C reach runs through major third-party marketplaces, so marketplace policy or demand shifts hit a core route to market. Mitigation cited: broadening institutional relationships, distributors and direct channels while monitoring channel economics.
- Low entry barriers and price competition — MD&A states low entry barriers and price competition may affect market share and margins — a structural feature of the automotive-accessories category, where the shift from unorganised to branded product is described as gradual. Mitigation cited: product quality, design differentiation, brand investment, service levels and speed to market.
- Rising finance cost and leverage — Management identifies the higher finance-cost burden as an important priority; the earnings growth rate trailed revenue growth partly because finance costs rose sharply, and the debt-equity ratio roughly doubled as borrowings increased relative to shareholders' funds. Strategy explicitly calls for aligning debt with the Group's operating cycle and for measured expansion.
- Operations and logistics dependence — Plant interruption, labour constraints, supplier delays or third-party logistics failures may affect delivery. The Company manufactures core products at a single described manufacturing facility and relies on third-party logistics. Mitigation cited: preventive maintenance, alternate sourcing, capacity planning and logistics performance reviews.
- Product quality and regulatory compliance — Product failure or non-compliance can lead to returns, claims and reputational harm — material for a consumer-facing accessories brand selling through marketplaces where returns and ratings affect visibility. Mitigation cited: quality checks, process controls, documentation and monitoring of applicable regulatory requirements.
- Technology shifts and changing consumer preferences — Changes in vehicle design, digital commerce or buyer preferences may make products or channels less relevant; vehicle-specific accessories must track new vehicle models and platforms. Mitigation cited: continuous product development, marketplace analytics and customer-feedback loops.
- Small scale and thin organisational depth; newly listed control environment — The Company had 39 employees on its rolls as at March 31, 2026, concentrating execution capacity in a small team. The Directors' Responsibility Statement records that, because the Company was not listed as at March 31, 2026, Section 134(5)(e) on internal financial controls of a listed company did not apply for the year under review, so the listed-company control regime applies only from FY27 following the May 29, 2026 SME listing.

business.body: Autofurnish designs, manufactures, markets and sells automotive accessories for cars and two-wheelers, with core offerings in vehicle body covers and foot mats alongside seat covers, cushions, sunshades, organizers, scooty mats, display protectors and trunk mats; it also trades in car utility products, audio accessories, lights, spare parts, interior accessories and dashboard products sourced from suppliers. The Company primarily serves business-to-business customers, distributors and trade channels, while its wholly owned subsidiary Golden Mace Private Limited addresses the direct-to-consumer market through major online marketplaces and the Group's own digital channels. The integrated model combines product design, sourcing, in-house manufacturing, brand management and distribution.

outlook.body:
- Deepen distribution in existing markets and selectively expand into underpenetrated domestic and international markets
- Introduce adjacent and premium products using customer feedback, design capability and category data

outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The annual report discloses no named capex project, capacity addition, commissioning timeline or site build-out. Expansion is described only in qualitative strategic terms: the Company manufactures its core products at its manufacturing facility (location and capacity not stated) and sources selected accessories from suppliers for trading and distribution. Management states the FY 2025-26 balance sheet and cash-flow profile call for measured expansion, with growth pursued with an emphasis on margin quality, working-capital efficiency and return on capital. The stated expansion levers are deepening distribution in existing markets and selectively expanding into underpenetrated domestic and international markets, introducing adjacent and premium products, and extending the portfolio into adjacent automotive-accessory categories using existing design, sourcing, manufacturing and distribution capabilities. The Managing Director lists strengthening manufacturing and sourcing capabilities among forward priorities (a stated intention, not a commissioned project). The only quantified capital event is financing rather than capex: subsequent to March 31, 2026 the Company completed an IPO of 35,61,000 equity shares of Rs 10 each at Rs 41 per share aggregating Rs 1,460.01 lakh and listed on the SME Platform of BSE Limited on May 29, 2026, described as providing additional resources to support future growth plans; the report in this bundle does not state the objects or deployment schedule of those proceeds. Conservation of energy and technology absorption are reported as 'Not applicable' under Section 134(3)(m), and there was no foreign exchange inflow or outflow during the year.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Growing vehicle parc: SIAM-reported growth across passenger vehicles, commercial vehicles, three-wheelers and two-wheelers in FY 2025-26 expands India's installed vehicle base and therefore the potential customer base for automotive accessories and aftermarket products
- Replacement and upgrade demand: body covers, foot mats and utility accessories draw demand both from new-vehicle purchasers and from existing owners seeking replacement or upgraded products
- Premiumisation and vehicle-specific products: rising consumer focus on protection, comfort, convenience, aesthetics and personalisation, plus preference for durable, better-designed accessories, supports a gradual shift from unorganised to organised and branded products
- Digital channel shift: growing use of online marketplaces and direct-to-consumer channels improves product discovery and price comparison and lets organised participants reach customers beyond traditional distribution networks without a matching physical-retail footprint
- Macro backdrop cited by management: IMF July 2026 projection of global growth of 3.0% in 2026 and 3.4% in 2027, and MoSPI provisional real GDP growth for FY 2025-26 of 7.7% (nominal 9.1%), providing a constructive backdrop for mobility-linked consumption
- Management states the addressable market expansion is subject to competitive intensity, fluctuations in input costs and changes in consumer spending
- Margin/cost levers flagged: earnings growth trailed revenue growth because employee benefit expense, finance costs and depreciation rose faster; the higher finance-cost burden and working-capital build remain management priorities
- Working-capital drivers: inventories and trade receivables rose materially on the higher operating base, so management focus is on demand-linked procurement, inventory turns, credit discipline and collections
- Opportunity set stated by management: vehicle-market expansion, organised and digital retail, product premiumisation, portfolio extension into adjacent automotive-accessory categories, and deeper institutional B2B relationships

group_structure.body: - Golden Mace Private Limited — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary of Autofurnish Limited (CIN U51909DL2016PTC304912). Per Form AOC-2, Autofurnish sells automotive accessories / goods to it in the ordinary course of business on an arm's length basis under a continuing commercial arrangement; the justification states the arrangement lets the Group use Golden Mace's direct-to-consumer and online distribution channels for wider market reach. No resolution under the first proviso to Section 188 was applicable (stated subject to confirmation from the Company's statutory records); no advances paid.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Manufactured automotive accessories:** Vehicle body covers, Car body covers, Bike accessories, Seat covers, Foot mats, Scooty mats, Cushions, Display protectors, Organizers, Sunshades, Trunk mats
- **Traded automotive accessories:** Car utility products, Audio accessories, Lights, Spare parts, Interior accessories, Dashboard products
- **Brands:** Autofurnish, Mototrance

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- India (the Group operates primarily in India; no separate geographic segment reported)
- Automotive aftermarket and accessories for cars and two-wheelers
- Business-to-business institutional and trade customers, distributors
- Direct-to-consumer via online marketplaces and own digital channels (through Golden Mace Private Limited)

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Growing vehicle parc: SIAM-reported growth across passenger vehicles, commercial vehicles, three-wheelers and two-wheelers in FY 2025-26 expands India's installed vehicle base and therefore the potential customer base for automotive accessories and aftermarket products
- Replacement and upgrade demand: body covers, foot mats and utility accessories draw demand both from new-vehicle purchasers and from existing owners seeking replacement or upgraded products
- Premiumisation and vehicle-specific products: rising consumer focus on protection, comfort, convenience, aesthetics and personalisation, plus preference for durable, better-designed accessories, supports a gradual shift from unorganised to organised and branded products
- Digital channel shift: growing use of online marketplaces and direct-to-consumer channels improves product discovery and price comparison and lets organised participants reach customers beyond traditional distribution networks without a matching physical-retail footprint
- Macro backdrop cited by management: IMF July 2026 projection of global growth of 3.0% in 2026 and 3.4% in 2027, and MoSPI provisional real GDP growth for FY 2025-26 of 7.7% (nominal 9.1%), providing a constructive backdrop for mobility-linked consumption
- Management states the addressable market expansion is subject to competitive intensity, fluctuations in input costs and changes in consumer spending
- Margin/cost levers flagged: earnings growth trailed revenue growth because employee benefit expense, finance costs and depreciation rose faster; the higher finance-cost burden and working-capital build remain management priorities
- Working-capital drivers: inventories and trade receivables rose materially on the higher operating base, so management focus is on demand-linked procurement, inventory turns, credit discipline and collections
- Opportunity set stated by management: vehicle-market expansion, organised and digital retail, product premiumisation, portfolio extension into adjacent automotive-accessory categories, and deeper institutional B2B relationships

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Deepen distribution in existing markets and selectively expand into underpenetrated domestic and international markets
- Introduce adjacent and premium products using customer feedback, design capability and category data
- Improve inventory productivity through forecasting, SKU rationalisation and closer linkage between procurement and demand
- Strengthen receivables management and cash conversion while aligning debt with the Group's operating cycle
- Use the enhanced visibility and capital-market access following the SME listing to support governance, brand building and disciplined growth
- Pursue measured expansion with an emphasis on margin quality, working-capital efficiency and return on capital, given the FY 2025-26 balance sheet and cash-flow profile
- Strengthen manufacturing and sourcing capabilities, broaden the product portfolio and improve operational efficiencies while expanding reach across traditional and digital distribution channels (MD's stated forward priorities)
- Operate complementary routes to market — the Company's B2B platform and Golden Mace's B2C e-commerce platform — rather than separate reported segments

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The annual report discloses no named capex project, capacity addition, commissioning timeline or site build-out. Expansion is described only in qualitative strategic terms: the Company manufactures its core products at its manufacturing facility (location and capacity not stated) and sources selected accessories from suppliers for trading and distribution. Management states the FY 2025-26 balance sheet and cash-flow profile call for measured expansion, with growth pursued with an emphasis on margin quality, working-capital efficiency and return on capital. The stated expansion levers are deepening distribution in existing markets and selectively expanding into underpenetrated domestic and international markets, introducing adjacent and premium products, and extending the portfolio into adjacent automotive-accessory categories using existing design, sourcing, manufacturing and distribution capabilities. The Managing Director lists strengthening manufacturing and sourcing capabilities among forward priorities (a stated intention, not a commissioned project). The only quantified capital event is financing rather than capex: subsequent to March 31, 2026 the Company completed an IPO of 35,61,000 equity shares of Rs 10 each at Rs 41 per share aggregating Rs 1,460.01 lakh and listed on the SME Platform of BSE Limited on May 29, 2026, described as providing additional resources to support future growth plans; the report in this bundle does not state the objects or deployment schedule of those proceeds. Conservation of energy and technology absorption are reported as 'Not applicable' under Section 134(3)(m), and there was no foreign exchange inflow or outflow during the year.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Integrated model combining product design, sourcing, manufacturing, brand management and distribution, allowing the Group to serve institutional and trade customers while using online channels to widen reach and gather consumer feedback
- Dual brand architecture — Autofurnish and Mototrance provide differentiated consumer propositions within the automotive-accessories category
- Complementary dual route to market: the Company's B2B platform plus Golden Mace's B2C e-commerce platform
- In-house production capabilities supported by sourced merchandise, balancing control, breadth and speed to market
- Established B2B capabilities described as a platform for deeper customer engagement, repeat business and broader product placement

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Working-capital intensity and funding dependence — MD&A flags that inventory and receivables can absorb cash and increase funding costs. Inventories and trade receivables rose materially during FY 2025-26 on the higher operating base, operating activities used cash rather than generating it, and funding requirements were met through financing inflows. Borrowings rose sharply, inventory-turnover, receivables-turnover and net-capital-turnover ratios all fell by more than 25%, and the debt-service coverage ratio fell on substantially increased debt-service obligations. Mitigation cited: SKU-level inventory discipline, customer credit controls, collections and cash-flow monitoring.
- Raw-material and merchandise cost volatility / supply disruption — Input-price volatility or supply disruption may compress margins or delay fulfilment. The business combines in-house manufacturing with sourced merchandise, so both manufacturing inputs and bought-in goods are exposed. Mitigation cited: supplier diversification, demand planning, negotiated procurement and selective price actions.
- Customer and channel concentration — Dependence on large customers or online marketplaces can affect volumes, pricing and visibility. The Company is primarily B2B while its subsidiary's B2C reach runs through major third-party marketplaces, so marketplace policy or demand shifts hit a core route to market. Mitigation cited: broadening institutional relationships, distributors and direct channels while monitoring channel economics.
- Low entry barriers and price competition — MD&A states low entry barriers and price competition may affect market share and margins — a structural feature of the automotive-accessories category, where the shift from unorganised to branded product is described as gradual. Mitigation cited: product quality, design differentiation, brand investment, service levels and speed to market.
- Rising finance cost and leverage — Management identifies the higher finance-cost burden as an important priority; the earnings growth rate trailed revenue growth partly because finance costs rose sharply, and the debt-equity ratio roughly doubled as borrowings increased relative to shareholders' funds. Strategy explicitly calls for aligning debt with the Group's operating cycle and for measured expansion.
- Operations and logistics dependence — Plant interruption, labour constraints, supplier delays or third-party logistics failures may affect delivery. The Company manufactures core products at a single described manufacturing facility and relies on third-party logistics. Mitigation cited: preventive maintenance, alternate sourcing, capacity planning and logistics performance reviews.
- Product quality and regulatory compliance — Product failure or non-compliance can lead to returns, claims and reputational harm — material for a consumer-facing accessories brand selling through marketplaces where returns and ratings affect visibility. Mitigation cited: quality checks, process controls, documentation and monitoring of applicable regulatory requirements.
- Technology shifts and changing consumer preferences — Changes in vehicle design, digital commerce or buyer preferences may make products or channels less relevant; vehicle-specific accessories must track new vehicle models and platforms. Mitigation cited: continuous product development, marketplace analytics and customer-feedback loops.
- Small scale and thin organisational depth; newly listed control environment — The Company had 39 employees on its rolls as at March 31, 2026, concentrating execution capacity in a small team. The Directors' Responsibility Statement records that, because the Company was not listed as at March 31, 2026, Section 134(5)(e) on internal financial controls of a listed company did not apply for the year under review, so the listed-company control regime applies only from FY27 following the May 29, 2026 SME listing.
